## Snapshot

This page records the validated CE-ARCH/CE-LIVE semantic baseline and the
completed physical repository consolidation against baseline commit:

```text
e02054fa103551c27f6a41907c49c6d923ce5777
```

Audit date:

```text
2026-08-28
```

The original 2026-08-21 audit remains useful historical context. CE-ARCH and
CE-LIVE are complete through native training, replay, concurrency, Tensor Core
non-promotion, and the CelleraTorch validation audit. The 2026-08-28 remap
changes physical ownership and build organization without changing those
semantic contracts.

The bounded post-remap completion pass then removed the CellShard reverse
runtime dependency, promoted the remaining fleet/reduction machinery into
`runtime/multi_gpu`, narrowed CellShard-backed public adapters under
`interop/cellshard`, and localized CMake target ownership. Compatibility names
remain available, but normal native targets no longer depend on the historical
`cellerator_compute_runtime` name.

## Repository-wide state

The repository now gives those generations distinct physical roles:

1. current execution, runtime, geometry, compute, planner, and interop
   implementation under canonical `include/Cellerator/` and `src/`
   ownership;
2. retained CP-Math v1 and legacy sparse evidence under `compat/`;
3. model and trajectory orchestration under `examples/` and Torch adaptation
   under `components/CelleraTorch`.

The documentation before this replacement described the first generation as the durable architecture, especially through Blocked-ELL-first and CellShard-backed sparse-ML language. That description is superseded.

### CE-LIVE activation state

CE-LIVE does not replace the completed CE-ARCH architecture. It now activates
one planner-backed quantitative path over it. The checksum-pinned PBMC3K
computational fixture runs through the executable program for widths 1, 16,
17, 31, 32, 48, and 64, three reuse horizons, and two mutable generations. The
bounded N=16 training program, CPE2/CPEXEC01 replay, event-based readiness,
fixed-transition CUDA Graph capture, and adversarial concurrency acceptance
are complete. Wave C evidence is recorded in
`bench/ce_live/evidence/ce_live_evidence_v1.json` and
`docs/CE_LIVE_EVIDENCE.md`.

The quantitative forward catalog currently offers exactly one legal FMP1 SpMM
schedule for each tested request. Its reported zero planner regret is therefore
complete over the legal set, but is not evidence of a universal win over
cuSPARSE. Training remains a small-module N=16 slice. The PBMC3K fixture is
computational evidence only. Tensor Core evaluation ended in measured
non-promotion. CelleraTorch is implemented as a thin optional native adapter;
its quantitative PBMC3K parity and bounded native autograd/readiness checks are
complete.

The retained CP-Math v1 surface is not the operation-core authority. Its
request, structural planner, prepared lifetime, and private runtime remain
migration-held compatibility evidence. New operations use the CE-ARCH
operation core and sole execution session.

### Default build boundary

The default CMake configure builds native Cellerator without entering the
CelleraTorch subdirectory or discovering Torch. The compatibility adapter is
available only through `-DCELLERATOR_ENABLE_TORCH_MODELS=ON`. This changes no
source ownership and deletes no legacy implementation.

`CELLERATOR_DEFAULT_SPARSE_LAYOUT` names only the fallback used by older
unspecified sparse surfaces. It is not a universal layout decision and does not
bypass operation-core candidate enumeration or complete-cost planning.

## CP-BP v1

CP-BP-01 through CP-BP-13 are implemented and closed.

### Construction pipeline

The source tree contains:

- deterministic sampling and sampled support;
- feature-major support bitsets;
- MinHash or related candidate discovery;
- exact merge-cost scoring;
- a constrained deterministic optimizer;
- frozen packing plans;
- full-partition plan application;
- compact cell-block records;
- bounded local cell ordering;
- host and CUDA warp-tile construction;
- alternating refinement;
- statistical validation;
- a hardware-cost model;
- persistent payload construction and rebinding.

### Native execution

The implemented direct CUDA operation is feature-weighted row reduction:

\[
y_r = \sum_f X_{r,f} w_f
\]

The kernel consumes device-resident CP-BP tiles directly.

Its v1 contract provides:

- one launch;
- no scratch;
- no allocation;
- no transfer;
- no device-wide synchronization;
- no CSR or BELL reconstruction;
- canonical-feature recovery;
- canonical partition-local output rows.

The last property is correct for the v1 API but should not become the future internal default.

### Operation-core activation

CE-ARCH-71 registers that preserved direct path as the
`cpbp-cpk1-row-masked-n1` operation-core candidate. The adapter is deliberately
narrow: it accepts only configured-precision, single-vector weighted relation
reduction over a prevalidated and device-rebound CPK1 row-masked projection.
Prepared state aliases immutable CPK1 geometry and canonical-row recovery
metadata. Relation values, feature weights, output storage, value generation,
stream, and zero-byte transient workspace remain launch bindings.

The candidate is deterministic and graph-capture compatible. It allocates,
copies, reconstructs, and synchronizes nothing, and calls the existing CP-BP
CUDA consumer directly. Its canonical row output preserves the v1 compatibility
contract; it is not a declaration that row-masked execution or canonical output
is the universal planner default.

CE-ARCH-72 registers the existing f16-value/f32-vector CSR path as the
`cellerator-csr-fallback-n1-f16-f32` conventional candidate under the same
operation-core contract. Preparation requires an already constructed,
device-resident CSR projection in packed feature order and aliases only its row
offsets and feature indices. Mutable relation values, dense input, output,
value generation, caller stream, and zero-byte workspace remain launch-bound.

The activated row-masked and CSR paths now have direct regression coverage for
multiple mutable value generations over one immutable relation structure and
one prepared structural execution. The proof keeps structure epoch, projection
geometry, and prepared state stable while changing value-plane generation and
allocation address; stale generations and real structure-epoch mismatches are
rejected before dispatch. Projection-kind mismatches remain explicit
preparation failures rather than triggering conversion or reconstruction.

The adapter launches the existing validated CSR kernel definition directly; it
does not construct CSR, allocate, copy, canonicalize, or synchronize in the hot
path. Projection construction and transfer remain explicit planner costs. The
candidate is deterministic but does not claim graph-capture support, and its
presence does not make CSR canonical or create another runtime.

CE-ARCH-73 connects real prepared candidates to the planner's empirical hook.
Each shortlisted candidate supplies a disposable output and a complete launch
binding on the caller/session stream. An untimed pipeline plus a neutral referee
establishes correctness before bounded warmup and sampling. CUDA events record
dynamic input packing, prepared execution, epilogue, output-order work, and
communication without device-wide synchronization or synchronization between
phases. Persistent semantic packing, projection construction, backend
preparation, static value packing, transfers, required synchronization, and
memory costs are recorded separately and amortized by their actual reuse keys.
The robust result is a median with median-absolute-deviation spread; planner
cache reuse still requires matching device-performance, runtime/build,
structure, geometry, projection, policy, and evidence-revision identities.
Autotuning never writes the caller-visible output, and unsupported or incorrect
candidates are rejected before their timings can affect selection.

CE-ARCH-75 adds `FMP1`, the first feature-major small-`N` physical projection
of the same frozen CP-BP structure. Projection construction transposes the
existing 32-row/32-feature mask grammar into per-tile packed-feature records,
participating-row masks, compact value offsets, and an exact source-value
position map. The pointer-free payload carries the persistent structure epoch,
`ProjectionId`, geometry identity, and execution-order identity and can be
stored as an ordinary CPE2 `native_feature_major` projection section. Mutable
generations are packed explicitly into FMP1-local order outside prepared
execution; neither geometry nor prepared state changes when a generation or
allocation address changes.

The registered `cpbp-feature-major-small-n-f16-f32` candidate accepts only
row-major packed f32 dense RHS/output with f16 relation values, f32 multiply and
accumulation, and `1 <= N <= 16`. One warp owns a row group, loads each
feature's `N`-wide dense vector once, and applies it to the masked participating
rows. Both output axes remain in their declared execution order, output is an
overwrite, and transient workspace is zero. Construction, value packing,
allocation, conversion, canonicalization, and synchronization are absent from
the run path. Correctness coverage includes partial tiles, irregular occupancy,
an empty row, both `N` boundaries, two value generations, identity/staleness
rejection, CPE2 prebinding, and the independent SpMM referee. Comparative
selection evidence remains owned by CE-ARCH-76.

### Historical V100 evidence

The recorded benchmark used:

- 65,536 rows;
- 32,768 features;
- 2,097,152 f16 nonzeros;
- resident input and output;
- three warmups;
- eleven repeats.

Median direct-tile times for high, medium, and low sharing were approximately:

```text
0.017 ms
0.041 ms
0.117 ms
```

The existing Cellerator CSR path measured approximately:

```text
0.075 ms
0.079 ms
0.095 ms
```

The result proves regime-dependent value:

- large win at high sharing;
- useful win at medium sharing;
- loss at low sharing.

No low-occupancy specialization met the recorded five-percent retention threshold. Low-sharing tiles therefore remain a measured fallback regime.

### Hardware cost model

The CP-BP-12 campaign measured 60 configurations and 120 paired direct-tile and CSR observations on V100.

Recorded held-out mean absolute percentage error was approximately:

```text
5.15 percent for direct tiles
5.88 percent for CSR
```

This is useful calibration evidence. The campaign used regular synthetic structures and the `N=1` operation, so it is not a complete core planner model.

### Persistence

CP-BP-13 adds:

- a 64-byte-aligned CPK1 pointer-free image;
- frozen plan maps;
- row order;
- warp tiles;
- semantic validation;
- host-to-device rebinding;
- direct runtime handoff.

CellShard wraps the opaque image in a versioned execution envelope and owns publication, compatibility checks, fetch, and contiguous upload.

CPK1 tightly reflects the v1 operation and projection. CPE2 provides the
sectioned execution-image container, projection directory, relocation, and
device prebinding around it and newer projections. CE-ARCH-82 completed Phase 4
by proving one unified CPK1-compatible, multi-value-plane, schema-extensible
path through direct prepared execution.

## Legacy CP-Math v1

This section describes the retained first-generation adapter surface. Its gaps
do not describe the CE-ARCH operation core completed below.

CP-Math v1 evidence now lives under:

```text
compat/cp_math_v1/include/Cellerator/compat/cp_math_v1/
compat/cp_math_v1/src/
tests/math_*.cc and tests/math_*.cu
bench/math/
```

### Implemented contracts

The public headers define:

- `spmm_request`;
- `spmm_bindings`;
- `math_request`;
- feature-order identity;
- sparse-structure identity;
- numeric storage, compute, and accumulation fields;
- transpose and dense layout;
- determinism;
- workspace policy;
- expected reuse;
- epilogue;
- operation signature;
- backend capability;
- pointer-free execution plan;
- backend registry;
- structural planner;
- device capabilities and fingerprint;
- device math context and workspace;
- prepared execution.

### Implemented physical and backend work

The tree contains:

- native tile adaptation;
- physical CSR lowering;
- physical BELL lowering;
- cuSPARSE CSR or BELL execution experiments;
- generic unfused epilogues;
- packed dense operand support;
- a CPU referee;
- contract, planner, runtime, lowering, execution, and epilogue tests.

### Compatibility build integration

The compatibility build exposes explicit evidence targets and the retained
packed-dense-operand benchmark. Historical include paths are forwarding
surfaces only; current implementation and current tests use canonical or
explicit compatibility paths. CP-Math v1 is not the execution owner for the
repository's sparse systems.

### Legacy adapter gaps

#### Prepared execution captures per-run state

`PreparedExecution` currently owns a `DeviceMathContext`, copies the full `math_request`, and retains current bindings. New dense input, output, bias, or stream generally implies a new preparation path.

The target architecture separates prepared immutable state from launch bindings.

#### Runtime context is duplicated

`DeviceMathContext` owns:

- an execution context;
- a CUDA stream;
- cuBLAS and cuSPARSE caches;
- one workspace allocation;
- device capabilities;
- device fingerprint.

Cellerator already has older runtime and sparse-operation contexts. These responsibilities must be unified.

#### Workspace is one reusable allocation

The current `WorkspacePool` is one resizable scratch arena with an allocation count and high watermark. It is not yet a concurrent stream-ordered pool with separate persistent and transient lifetimes.

#### Planning is structural

The planner enumerates legal backend candidates and performs inexpensive structural pruning. Its own comments defer measured selection and persistence to an external autotuner or cache owner.

The target core requires one integrated cost and measurement system.

#### Operation scope is narrow

The operation enum currently contains SpMM. The future core must also represent reductions, graph propagation, sequence-conditioned operations, sparse-to-dense projections, recurrent updates, and fused programs.

#### Identity is partial

Feature-order and sparse-structure identities are useful beginnings. They do not yet provide universal domain, row order, geometry, partition, structure epoch, and value-generation identity.

#### Numeric policy is incomplete

The request distinguishes storage, compute, and accumulation codes, but current scalar, bias, backend, and legal-tuple behavior does not yet form a complete mixed-precision contract.

#### Padded BELL risk

The physical BELL view records logical and padded dimensions. The vendor descriptor may use padded dimensions while generic bindings expose logical-sized dense input and output buffers.

Until the backend owns padded B and C buffers with explicit pack and crop, or rejects mismatched padded dimensions, this is a correctness risk.

Aligned tests do not establish safety for unaligned logical dimensions.

## Existing sparse and model systems

The repository also contains useful existing systems:

- CSR and compressed sparse operations;
- Blocked-ELL;
- SELL and sliced execution;
- quantized Blocked-ELL;
- generic sparse row transforms and column moments used by downstream BioPrep;
- exact neighbor search;
- trajectory logic;
- native model implementations;
- distributed and NCCL paths;
- CelleraTorch adapters.

These systems are not discarded.

They should become:

- planner candidates;
- fallback projections;
- reference implementations;
- realistic benchmark workloads;
- migration adapters.

Their current ownership and assumptions do not define the final core.

## Baseplane

Baseplane currently provides:

- two-bit nucleotide packing;
- packed-word and 32-base plane representations;
- reverse complements;
- mismatch and motif-window operations;
- exact count and compact emit;
- resident plane streams;
- base, GC, and CpG masks;
- CPU, SIMD, and CUDA paths;
- allocation-free hot APIs with caller-owned output.

The following were the integration limitations at the original audit:

- validity and ambiguous-base policy must be mandatory and explicit;
- tail validity must travel with plane streams;
- local and global coordinate widths need a stable chunk contract;
- motif plans must be normalized and immutable;
- output ordering and overflow semantics need stronger contracts;
- the shared predicate ABI and operand identities do not yet constitute the
  complete direct relation-builder contract required by Phase 10;
- CE-ARCH-78 records a fused-versus-reused-materialization crossover, but the
  complete-cost choice is not yet integrated across the full relation-builder
  and repeated-state program.

## Documentation state before replacement

Previous repository documentation contained several conflicting claims:

- Blocked-ELL as the universal preferred sparse layout;
- CellShard as the owner of layout derivation;
- Cellerator as primarily sparse ML over CellShard matrices;
- Baseplane as an external provider of bit primitives;
- root strategy files as architecture authority;
- closed TODO ledgers as pickup guidance.

Several root documents also referenced missing files such as `pointer_migration_plan.md`.

The replacement documentation removes those assumptions from the active guidance.

## CE-ARCH completion state

### Closed continuation

CE-ARCH-81 through CE-ARCH-92 close roadmap Phases 4 through 11 and the final
evidence audit:

- CE-ARCH-81: truthful roadmap and executable status matrix;
- CE-ARCH-82: unified Execution Image v2 compatibility/runtime closure;
- CE-ARCH-83: representative instrumentation and benchmark corpus;
- CE-ARCH-84: missing low-sharing/tail and CTA-scale forward regimes;
- CE-ARCH-85: transpose projection and native backward;
- CE-ARCH-86: connected-operation planning;
- CE-ARCH-87: full Objective V2 CP-BP refinement integration;
- CE-ARCH-88: native sparse-to-dense training vertical slice;
- CE-ARCH-89: complete Baseplane relation/fusion integration;
- CE-ARCH-90: hierarchy and scale-out readiness;
- CE-ARCH-91: opaque CellShard artifact delivery across the existing
  CSPACK/CPEXEC01 compatibility boundary;
- CE-ARCH-92: real-data regime evidence and migration-completion audit.

The CE-ARCH-92 campaign compares row-masked, CSR, feature-major warp, and
feature-major CTA execution over full GSE147520 and PBMC3K support traces, a
checksum-pinned high-sharing slice derived from GSE147520, and an adversarial
partial-block trace at N=1/16/32. It records 36 correct candidate results with
at most 2.05% median-absolute-deviation spread. At the declared eight-use
horizon, row-masked wins the real high-sharing N=1 slice, CSR wins the full real
supports at N=1, and feature-major wins every N=16/32 cell. The canonical
summary is `bench/architecture_evidence/ce_arch_92_v100_summary.json`; CUDA
controller evidence `490d2ba1-99ce-4d3e-ba1c-65db915a42d1` preserves the
serialized V100 run and exact source/binary identity.

The completion statement is deliberately bounded. It does not complete the
independent CS-FOUND roadmap, claim future Tensor Core or distributed candidate
families, or turn the current Objective V2 calibration into a permanent law.
Empirical measurement remains authoritative for uncertain and novel regimes.

The phase-by-phase canonical evidence matrix and exact completion definition are
in `migration_roadmap.qmd`.

## CE-PTR integrated state

The 2026-08-29 CE-PTR integration adds the frozen memory substrate and explicit
session/image/workspace contracts, CPI1 frozen plans, exact geometry build
relations, prepared optimizer slabs and journals, deterministic sampling and
statistical images, a resident support-to-candidate pipeline, flattened graph
relations, capacity-specialized exact search, caller-owned forward-neighbor
views, and exact projection-construction workspaces. Native forward-neighbor
targets no longer link CellShard runtime ownership; index persistence, staging,
and workflow policy remain downstream.

The final production inventory is intentionally transitional: 169 controlled
owning-family spellings remain under exact non-increasing ceilings, plus live
`host_buffer` and trajectory batch compatibility helpers not covered by the
lexical families. The legacy `device_buffer` still offers blocking helpers.
Those surfaces are not evidence that prepared execution may allocate or
synchronize; only the tested sealed/session APIs carry that promise. The
authoritative final counts, dispositions, and direct validation commands are in
`CE_PTR_INVENTORY.md` and `bench/ce_ptr/final/acceptance.md`.

## CE-GEO integrated implementation

The normal build now owns the common NVIDIA physical realization, `sm_70`
provider manifest, N=64 value pack/MMA/residual/epilogue path, relation catalog
assembly, generic segment primitives, transpose relation apply, support
contraction, logical-edge gradients, and prepared biological exchange
composition. A 4-binary vertical suite and 14-binary biology suite are part of
the normal build graph. The final validation rebuilt native Release `sm_70`
and explicit Torch-compatibility configurations and passed all 22 acceptance
commands. Compute Sanitizer passed 22/22 runs after fixing a real shared-scratch
reuse race in segment normalization.

The implementation remains intentionally bounded. Whole-exchange fusion is
`evaluated_not_promoted`; width sweeps outside the promoted N=64 exact-cover
regime are calibration evidence; profiler cache/stall counters were unavailable
for that sweep; and the preprint ablations are synthetic mechanism controls,
not biological performance claims.
